title: Tenali Raman and the Mysterious Footprints

full_text:
A wealthy silk importer named Dhananjaya was burgled overnight of three heavy bolts of imported Chinese gold-woven damask, each bolt weighing thirty pounds.
The theft occurred during a brief monsoon shower that had softened the red clay pathway outside the warehouse.
The city police were baffled: the thief had covered his face and worn no distinctive shoes.

Tenali Raman was invited to inspect the crime scene.
Tenali examined the red clay path.
In the soft mud, there was a single set of bare human footprints leading away from the warehouse door toward the northern highway.
Tenali knelt, measured the footprints with a bamboo ruler, and examined their depth:

'Notice three things,' Tenali said to the King and the police captain:
'First: The footprint shows that the left foot is pressed far deeper into the mud than the right foot. A man who carries an uneven load over his left shoulder naturally presses harder with his left foot to maintain balance.
Second: The toes of the left foot are turned outwards at an angle of thirty degrees, while the heel is unusually narrow, indicating that the carrier walks with a slight habitual limp in his left hip.
Third: Along the path, every fifty paces, the walker stopped and leaned against a tree, leaving the distinctive circular indentation of a heavy round iron-shod walking stick!'

The police captain scratched his head: 'There are thousands of men in Vijayanagara, Tenali; how does this help us?'

Tenali smiled: 'We need not search the city; we need only check the palace porter registry for a man who limps in his left hip, uses an iron-shod staff, and has broad shoulders capable of carrying ninety pounds of fabric!'

The registry revealed only one match: a former palace porter named Somanna, who had retired with a hip injury.
Tenali and the guards marched to Somanna’s cottage.
Behind the stable, buried under dry hay, were the three stolen bolts of Chinese gold-woven damask!
Somanna’s iron-shod staff stood beside the door, matching the circular indentations in the mud with millimeter precision!

Somanna fell to his knees, confessing that a rival merchant had paid him to steal the cloth.
The silk was returned to Dhananjaya, and the King marveled at Tenali’s extraordinary forensic deduction:
'Tenali, while others saw only mud, thou didst read a complete portrait of the thief from his footprints!'
moral: Forensic observation of gait, depth, and weight solves crimes that leave no eyewitnesses.
